comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
READ-ONLY DIAGNOSIS from a non-owning session (no claim, no edits, no gates run). Comment only.

Question asked: why does scanner-integration actually fail? Answer: there are THREE distinct
faults, not two. The third has never been named, and the revert commit's stated diagnosis of it
is wrong.

== FAULT 1 (already known) — missing script on old-base patchsets ==
gerrit-verify.yaml resolves the reusable workflow from TRUSTED MAIN but checks out the
PATCHSET, so `make`/`scripts/` come from the patchset. A patchset whose base predates
6125c5345f01 has no scripts/install_review_scanners.py.
Measured, job 100953010259 (run 33848388672, change 2594/3):
  python: can't open file '/home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/scripts/install_review_scanners.py':
  [Errno 2] No such file or directory
This explains ONLY the old-base lane.

== FAULT 2 (found, and already fixed on main) — dash has no `pipefail` ==
Makefile `scanner-integration` opened with `set -euo pipefail`. GNU make runs recipes under
/bin/sh, which is dash on ubuntu-latest.
Measured on MAIN ITSELF, job 100919632441 (workflow_dispatch run 33839813271):
  review scanner locks: OK
  /bin/sh: 1: set: Illegal option -o pipefail
  make: *** [Makefile:475: scanner-integration] Error 2
  ##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.
Note `validate-locks` PASSES ("review scanner locks: OK"); the failure is the very first line of
the make recipe. That is why the job dies in ~30-50s. Also measured on a patchset lane, job
100941048312. Fixed on main by 6b034b9f8224 (`set -euo pipefail` -> `set -eu`, Makefile:500).

== FAULT 3 (NEW — this is the one nobody had) — dangling RELATIVE semgrep symlink ==
Once fault 2 was fixed, the job got further and failed differently. Measured, job 100935522585
(run 33844923442), against the FIXED Makefile (note "Makefile:500", not 475):
  Successfully installed ... semgrep-1.145.0
  [notice] To update, run: /home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/.tools/review-scanners/semgrep-venv/bin/python3.12 -m pip install --upgrade pip
  ERROR: could not execute .tools/review-scanners/bin/semgrep: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.tools/review-scanners/bin/semgrep'
  make: *** [Makefile:500: scanner-integration] Error 2

Mechanism, with citations (paths absolute; line numbers as of 6b034b9f8224):
- /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/Makefile:503 passes a RELATIVE prefix:
  `--prefix "$(REVIEW_SCANNER_PREFIX)"` where REVIEW_SCANNER_PREFIX := .tools/review-scanners
  (Makefile:52). By contrast /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/scripts/install_review_scanners.py:22
  DEFAULT_PREFIX is ABSOLUTE (REPO_ROOT-derived).
- install_scanners (scripts/install_review_scanners.py:342-354):
    semgrep = _install_semgrep(entry, semgrep_venv or prefix / "semgrep-venv")   # line 351
    semgrep_link = _link_semgrep(semgrep, prefix)                                # line 352
    _run_version(semgrep_link, entry.semgrep_version)                            # line 354
  With a relative prefix, `semgrep` is the RELATIVE path
  `.tools/review-scanners/semgrep-venv/bin/semgrep`.
- _link_semgrep (scripts/install_review_scanners.py:328-339) does
  `link.symlink_to(semgrep)` at line 335, where link is
  `.tools/review-scanners/bin/semgrep`. A relative symlink target is resolved relative to the
  symlink's OWN DIRECTORY, so the link resolves to
  `.tools/review-scanners/bin/.tools/review-scanners/semgrep-venv/bin/semgrep` — nonexistent.
  The symlink is created successfully and DANGLES.
- _run_version (scripts/install_review_scanners.py:287-297) execs it, catches OSError at 296 and
  raises `could not execute {binary}: {exc}` — exactly the CI string above.
- Gitleaks is unaffected because _install_gitleaks uses `shutil.copy2` (a real copy), not a
  symlink. That is precisely why gitleaks passes and semgrep fails.

Reproduced deterministically in a throwaway tmpdir (no repo touched), identical error shape:
  link target: .t/rs/semgrep-venv/bin/semgrep
  link exists() -> False
  could not execute .t/rs/bin/semgrep: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.t/rs/bin/semgrep'

IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the revert commit 9c7d78127696 states "the underlying scanner contract step
(pytest SCANNER_INTEGRATION_NODES) fails on every change". That is NOT what the logs show. pytest
NEVER RAN. Execution died inside the `install` step's own post-install version verification
(Makefile:503), before the `check` at 504 and before pytest at 506. The scanner contracts are
untested, not failing — the distinction matters for the follow-up ticket, because it means we
still have zero evidence about whether the nine contracts pass.

This also explains why nobody caught it locally: `python scripts/install_review_scanners.py
install` with NO --prefix uses the ABSOLUTE DEFAULT_PREFIX and works fine. Only the Makefile path,
which passes a relative prefix, is broken. The bug is latent in every prefix-override call site.

== BRANCH-HEAD `skipped` vs PATCHSET `failure` ==
Not a clue about conditions/inputs — it is the documented schedule guard.
/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.github/workflows/test.yml:77-79:
    scanner-integration:
      if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
      uses: ./.github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml
The branch-head runs being observed are the scheduled main-health runs. Measured: run 33846424069
has `event = schedule`, headSha 6b034b9f8224, and reports scanner-integration = skipped —
alongside `mutation = skipped`, which carries the same guard (test.yml:71-73). The Gerrit lane
(gerrit-verify.yaml:241-253) has no schedule guard, so it runs and fails. The `skipped` seen in
the docs-only Verified route is a THIRD, separate and intentional thing
(gerrit-verify.yaml:490 asserts scanner-integration.result == 'skipped').

== ON THE TWO ITEMS FLAGGED BY 2595's OWN LLM REVIEW ==
Examined; both are real defects but NEITHER is this failure.
- `--install-dir` honoured on install but not check: _selected_prefix
  (install_review_scanners.py:376-379) IS applied on both paths in main() (:399, :409-410), so
  the original complaint is stale as written. The live inconsistency is elsewhere:
  main() line 405 passes `_selected_prefix(args)` to check_scanners, while --check-only at :392
  also does — consistent. Ruled out as the cause: CI never passes --install-dir.
- `--semgrep-venv` declared but never read: it IS read, at main():406 -> install_scanners's
  `semgrep_venv` kwarg (:347, :351). Stale finding. Ruled out: CI never passes it.

== WHAT A CORRECT FIX LOOKS LIKE (not implemented here) ==
The minimal, targeted repair is one line in _link_semgrep: make the symlink target absolute.
    link.symlink_to(semgrep.resolve())      # install_review_scanners.py:335
Belt-and-braces alternative that fixes the whole class rather than the one site: resolve the
prefix once at the boundary, e.g. have _selected_prefix (:376) return `.resolve()`, so every
downstream path (bin dir, semgrep-venv, gitleaks work dir, the check path) is absolute regardless
of how the caller spelled --prefix. I'd favour this one; the relative-prefix hazard is latent in
every override call site, not just the symlink.
Either way, add a regression test that invokes the installer with a RELATIVE --prefix from a
different cwd and asserts the resulting bin/semgrep is executable — that is the exact gap the
existing tests miss, since they exercise the absolute DEFAULT_PREFIX.

Separately, and independent of the symlink: re-landing this lane must not repeat the vacuous
vote. 6125c5345f01's own Verified run 33831682168 contains 26 jobs and NO scanner-integration
job, because the Verified lane runs gerrit-verify.yaml from trusted main, which did not yet
define it. Any re-land needs the lane proven green on a real patchset before it becomes required.

Also still unknown after the fix: whether the nine SCANNER_INTEGRATION_NODES contracts actually
pass. No run has ever reached them. Treat that as open, not as a known failure.

Current state at time of writing: main is 9c7d78127696 ("Revert scanner-integration Verified
gate"), which removes the workflow, the script, the locks and the Makefile target, so the
immediate freeze is lifted.

`6125c5345f01` (Gerrit 2595, ticket aa9e), casts `Verified -1` on effectively every change pushed
since it merged, blocking all merges.

**Root fault (Defect 1), quoted from a real job log** (branch-head lane, run 33834183836 job
100903189596, a tree that carries the scanner script):

```
review scanner locks: OK
/bin/sh: 1: set: Illegal option -o pipefail
make: *** [Makefile: scanner-integration] Error 2
```

The `scanner-integration` recipe opens with `@set -euo pipefail;`. The Makefile sets no `SHELL`, so
GNU make runs the recipe under `/bin/sh` — dash on ubuntu-latest, which has no `pipefail`.
`set -o pipefail` is a dash **runtime** error at the `set` builtin (NOT a parse error — `dash -n`
does not validate `set` option arguments). The recipe body contains no pipeline, so `pipefail` is
inert.

**Exact location (current tree, rebased on Gerrit 2600, which shifted Makefile line numbers):** the
`scanner-integration` recipe header is at **Makefile:499** and the offending `@set -euo pipefail;`
is at **Makefile:500**. (The quoted log's `Makefile:475` reflects the pre-2600 revision; the line
has since moved to 500.)

**How it landed broken.** 2595's own Verified run 33831682168 contains 26 jobs and NO
`scanner-integration` job at all: the Verified lane runs `gerrit-verify.yaml` from trusted `main`,
which did not yet wire the lane, so 2595's `+1` was cast without the new job ever executing.

## Approach

Replace `set -euo pipefail` with POSIX `set -eu` in the `scanner-integration` recipe (Makefile:500).
The recipe has no pipeline, so this is behaviour-preserving under bash and correct under dash. It is
a one-line change and introduces no new script, config key, env var, feature flag, or lock, so the
mechanism-delta ratchet sees nothing new.

Stacked on Gerrit 2600 so this change's OWN Verified run exercises the (now-fixed)
`scanner-integration` job on a tree that carries the scanner script — so, unlike 2595, this change
is validated by the very job it repairs.

## Scope

- `Makefile` — the `scanner-integration` recipe's `set` line (Makefile:500) only.

## Deferred to follow-up b973-b298-9b5d-4765 (discovered_from this ticket)

Intentionally OUT of scope for this incident fix:
- Defect 2: `_scanner-integration.yml` lacks the `[ -f scripts/install_review_scanners.py ]`
  predates-gate guard, so a change based before `6125c534` fails `No such file` until rebased.
- The vacuous-vote escape closure: derive `test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py`'s guarded set from
  the `gerrit-verify.yaml`/`test.yml` local-`uses:` closure, plus a STATIC bash-only-construct scan
  over CI-reachable make recipes (a parse-only `dash -n` check does not catch `set -o pipefail`).

## Testing

- Defect-seeded RED/GREEN (executable, portable, no CI provider required): `sh -c 'set -euo pipefail'`
  exits nonzero with `Illegal option -o pipefail` — the exact production failure — while
  `sh -c 'set -eu'` exits 0. Verified locally under dash. (Executing the leading `set` line under
  dash is a valid detection oracle; a parse-only check is not.)
- No-pipeline check: the recipe body (Makefile:500-506) contains no `|`, confirming `pipefail` was
  inert and the change is behaviour-preserving.
- Integration proof: this change's own `scanner-integration` Verified job reaches `+1` (green),
  where it was `-1` on every change before the fix.
- Verification set: `make lint`, `make typecheck`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The `scanner-integration` recipe at Makefile:500 reads `@set -eu;` (was `@set -euo pipefail;`);
      the citation matches the actual recipe location (header Makefile:499). Checked by reading the diff.
- [ ] Defect-seeded RED/GREEN recorded: `sh -c 'set -euo pipefail'` fails with `Illegal option -o
      pipefail` and `sh -c 'set -eu'` succeeds. Checked by the quoted shell output in a ticket comment.
- [ ] The `scanner-integration` Verified job passes on this change (was red on every change since
      `6125c534`). Checked by this change reaching `Verified +1` with the `scanner-integration` job green.
- [ ] No new mechanism is introduced (no script/config/env/flag/lock). Checked by the mechanism-delta
      ratchet staying green in `make lint`.
- [ ] The two deferred hardening items are captured in linked follow-up b973-b298-9b5d-4765. Checked
      by the `discovered_from` link.
